chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Rizaqallah ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Suleyman ibn Umar al-Sarraj, from one of our companions, who said:
The clay of the grave of Al-Hus-Husayn (peace be upon him) is taken from near the grave up to a distance of seventy cubits.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on taking clay from the grave of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the unique spiritual status of the soil surrounding Imam Al-Husayn’s (peace be upon him) grave in Karbala, specifying a radius of seventy cubits for its distinctiveness. In Shia tradition, this specific measurement underscores the sanctity of the site, often linking the earth itself to the Imam’s enduring presence and serving as a medium for barakah (blessing) and healing. The ruling reflects the broader theological concept of the physical world being imbued with sacredness through the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Razaqallah Bin Abu Al A’ala, from Suleyman Bin Umar Al Sarraj, from one of our companions who said,
‘You can take the clay of the grave of Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> from the grave up to (a distance of) seventy cubits’ (70 square yards).
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Rizq Allah ibn abu al-‘Ala’ from Sulayman ibn ‘Umar al-Sarraj from certain individuals of our people who has said the following: “
Clay of the grave of al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, can be taken from within a seventy square yard area.”
